items.title: जिस सीट पर केजरीवाल मामूली अंतर से हारे, वहां 2025 चुनाव से पहले जुड़े 40 फीसदी नाम एसआईआर के ड्राफ्ट में गायब
items.summary: नई दिल्ली विधानसभा क्षेत्र में ‘ब्लाइंड रिलीफ एसोसिएशन’ के कैंपस में जनवरी 2025 में मतदाता सूची में जोड़े गए 10 वोटरों के नाम अब हटा दिए गए हैं. ये नाम विधानसभा चुनाव से करीब एक महीने पहले जोड़े गए थे. इन्हें हटाए जाने की वजह “स्थायी रूप से स्थानांतरित” के तौर पर दर्ज की गई है. गौरतलब है कि ये सभी इस संस्था के रेजिडेंशियल स्टूडेंट थे. यह संस्था एक सीनियर सेकेंडरी स्कूल और वोकेशनल ट्रेनिंग सेंटर चलाती है. यहां स्किलिंग से जुड़े कोर्स कराए जाते हैं. एनजीओ के एग्जीक्यूटिव सेक्रेटरी डेविड अब्सालोम ने बताया कि 2025 के चुनाव से पहले जिला प्रशासन ने संस्था से संपर्क कर दृष्टिबाधित छात्रों के लिए एक विशेष कैंप लगाने की बात कही थी. संस्था में प्रशासनिक कर्मचारी तेजिंदर सिंह बिष्ट ने बताया कि चुनाव अधिकारियों के साथ संस्था की लंबे समय से बातचीत चल रही थी. उल्लेखनीय है कि चुनाव आयोग के मैनुअल में हॉस्टल में रहने वाले छात्रों को मतदाता के तौर पर पंजीकरण कराने की अनुमति है. यह ‘ऑर्डिनरिली रेजिडेंट’ यानी सामान्य तौर पर निवासी की शर्त पूरी करने के पात्र हो सकते हैं, बशर्ते उनका items.title: Doctored ‘bikini in Ganga’ video goes viral; News18 runs it without verification
items.summary: The story uses screenshots and not the actual viral video in view of its sensitive nature. A 12-second long video is going viral on social media where a woman is seen bathing in river water while wearing a bikini. The video was posted on September 15 by X user Barkha Trehan, who describes herself as ‘Activist | Voice Of Men | President, Purush Aayog’. She wrote, “Location : Haridwar. Madam: My Body My Choice. Your take ??” The video garnered over 1 million views. ( Archive ) In her X bio, Trehan identifies herself as a “men’s rights activist” and the “president of Purush Aayog”. She also claims to be a TEDx speaker and a “Hindu entrepreneur”; she apparently also “directed a documentary titled The Curse of Manhood”. Media outlet News 18 Hindi published a report with screenshots from the video pointing out that it had angered social media users. ( Archive ) This same video was posted by content creator Piyali Banerjee, where she questioned the “basic decency” and “knowledge of clothing” of the woman. Other social media users also shared the same video with similar captions, questing the woman for wearing a bikini in Haridwar, with misogynistic comments about her character. The video is also viral on Instagram . Fact Check To verify its authenticity, we ran a reverse image search on a few keyframes from the viral clip. This search led us to a reel posted on Instagram on August 18. The 21-second-long reel was uploaded by an account named ‘ishika_pandit’. It showed the same woman bathing at the same spot, but wearing completely different clothes. View this post on Instagram A post shared by ब्रह्माणी (@ishika_pandiit) This video matched the background of the viral clip with the steel railing on the river and the foundations of a bridge clearly visible in the background. The woman’s hand gestures also mirror the viral video, and the same two men are visible in both videos. Based on these similarities, it can be concluded that the video uploaded on August 18 is the original footage. The woman in the original video is seen wearing a yellow suit, and not a bikini. Thus, the viral clip is a doctored version of the original video, manipulating the attire of the woman. Some social media users highlighted the possibility of the viral clip being an AI-generated deepfake, claiming that the woman’s clothes had been purposely changed from a suit to a bikini. items.summary: At the Blind Relief Association campus in the New Delhi constituency, 10 voters who were added to the electoral roll in January 2025, a month before the assembly elections, have now been removed. The reason recorded for their deletion: “permanently shifted.” They were residential students at the NGO, which runs a senior secondary school and a vocational training centre with skilling courses. David Absalom, the NGO’s executive secretary, said that ahead of the 2025 elections, the district administration had approached the organisation to hold a special camp for visually impaired students. Tejinder Singh Bisht, an administrative staff member, said the organisation had long been in discussions with poll officials. The Election Commission’s own manual allows hostel students to register as voters and to qualify under the ordinarily resident clause, provided the course runs for at least a year and is recognised by a government, board or university. But there were two reasons why these students were deleted: one, because most of them were now registered as voters outside Delhi, and two, their residential skilling course was already complete when the enumeration phase was still underway. They could not be reached for comment. Of the 1,430 voters added in January 2025, 560 – nearly four in 10 – have been deleted. Of the 2,369 added in December 2024, 783, or roughly a third, have gone the same way. The constituency – from where AAP’s Arvind Kejriwal lost with a thin margin to BJP’s Pravesh Verma in 2025 – had 1,08,788 electors during the assembly elections. The SIR removed 37,315 of them, a deletion rate of about 34.3 percent. Between January 2025 and June 2026, before the SIR even began, the constituency had already recorded 25,185 deletions against just 5,713 additions. Add the SIR’s own 37,315 removals, and the constituency has lost a total of 62,500 voters since the 2025 elections. Between the 2025 assembly elections and the start of the SIR, 11.1 lakh voters were removed from the state’s rolls. The SIR itself deleted another 47.5 lakh. items.title: Centre supports plea in Delhi HC to allow same-sex partners be medical representatives for each other
items.summary: The Central government in its affidavit before the Delhi High Court has backed a plea seeking directions to hospitals and doctors to recognise same-sex partners as each other’s medical representatives, allowing them to give consent for medical treatment during health emergencies. In the affidavit dated September 10, the Central government stated that the plea to recognise a non-heterosexual partner as a medical representative is "substantially capable of being accommodated" within the existing legal and ethical framework. It stated that the provisions of Indian Medical Council (Professional · Conduct, Etiquette and Ethics) Regulations, 2002 may be harmoniously read so as not to exclude people merely on account of sexual orientation. The Centre stated that the absence of a relative should not by itself prevent urgent medical treatment. It added that an administrative practice of insisting upon consent of a relative cannot ordinarily override a competent adult patient's right to bodily autonomy. Further, it is stated in the affidavit that factors such as the nature of the treatment, urgency of the medical situation, patient's own wishes are relevant considerations in determining the medical representative. The plea was filed by a woman who got married to her partner in New Zealand in 2023. She argued that there is a critical need for recognition of their union in the medical context, particularly because her partners' immediate family members reside in different states or countries, making them potentially inaccessible during a medical emergency. It was contended that the existing regulations mandate consent of "husband or wife, parent or guardian in case of minors, or the patient himself" for medical procedures or treatment. "This lack of explicit recognition of partners in a union renders the Petitioner effectively powerless to make critical medical decisions for Ms. Chopra, or vice-a-versa, a right readily available to heterosexual partners/couples under the prevailing 2002 Regulations," the plea said. It added that prevailing legal and regulatory classification violates homosexual people's rights under Articles 14, 15, 19 and 21 of the Constitution of India. items.title: Plea in Supreme Court challenges Centre's decision to levy MDR on merchant UPI transactions over ₹2,000
items.summary: A Public Interest Litigation (PIL) has been filed before the Supreme Court challenging the Central government's decision to withdraw the statutory zero-Merchant Discount Rate (MDR) protection for Unified Payments Interface (UPI) transactions exceeding ₹2,000 [ Anjan Datta v. Union of India ]. The petition assails the proposed MDR framework scheduled to take effect from October 15, 2026. It highlights that while UPI payments above ₹2,000 have been exposed to levies, identical "no-charge" protection continues to be extended to RuPay-powered debit cards without any monetary ceiling. While clarifying that the challenge is not to maintaining secure payment infrastructure, the plea assails the creation of a nationwide compulsory payment burden without disclosing cost studies, underlying methodology, or enforceable anti-pass-through safeguards. Under the announced framework, person-to-person (P2P) transfers and person-to-merchant (P2M) payments up to ₹2,000 remain free. However, a 0.4% MDR applies to P2M payments above ₹2,000, with transactions of ₹75,000 and above capped at ₹300. Specified essential sectors attract a flat ₹5 charge, capital-market payments carry a 0.02% levy and merchants receiving up to ₹1 lakh per month remain exempt. The petition argues that despite official assertions that merchants cannot pass these costs to consumers, the fee on qualifying receipts will inevitably enter price structures, reduce working capital, or induce refusal of UPI payments and transaction-splitting among low-margin traders. "A bare direction against an expressly recognised economic consequence does not eliminate the burden," the plea asserts. The PIL, filed by Advocate Anjan Datta, further contends that thresholds like the ₹2,000 transaction mark and ₹1 lakh monthly receipt ceiling are unsupported by disclosed data. A transaction of ₹2,001 attracts a percentage fee while ₹2,000 does not, creating financial "cliffs" that distort market behaviour and discriminate between similarly situated merchants while favouring very high-value transactions via the cap, it says. Assailing the multi-tiered levy as manifestly arbitrary and violative of Articles 14 and 19(1)(g) of the Constitution, the petitioner argues that fixing financial charges via press releases rather than notified statutory rules suffers from excessive delegation of essential fiscal functions to an unincorporated steering committee. items.title: Delhi HC questions Delhi government on fire rules allowing private auditors to certify building safety
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Wednesday issued notice to the Delhi government, the Delhi Fire Service and the Lieutenant Governor’s office on a plea challenging the changes made in the law that replace mandatory inspections by government fire officers with fire safety certifications by private auditors engaged and paid by building owners. A Division Bench of Chief Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya and Justice Tejas Karia questioned the government on how it can delegate the government’s essential functions to third parties. “You are delegating your essential functions. Is this permitted? This is the essential function of the fire department. Can you delegate it? There is a problem,” the Court remarked. It directed the authorities to file their replies in 4 weeks and said that the case will be heard next on December 12. Chief Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya and Justice Tejas Karia The High Court was hearing a public interest litigation (PIL) filed by Umed Singh Chhillar, an 84-year-old former Indian Army serviceman and retired Delhi Fire Service officer associated with the Institution of Fire Engineers (India). Chhillar has challenged the amendment to the Delhi Fire Service Act, 2007, saying that the recently notified Delhi Fire Service (Amendment) Rules, 2026 dilute safeguards concerning fire and life safety in Delhi. The petition contends that the new framework allows building owners to engage private fire safety auditors, while insulating the Delhi Fire Service from liability for losses arising from such certifications. It further challenges provisions making fire safety certificates effectively perpetual, subject to annual self-declarations, instead of time-bound renewal inspections. The plea also alleges that the amendments exceed the rule-making power under Section 63 of the 2007 Act and remove references to the National Building Code, which provides guidelines for regulating building construction activities. Citing recent fires in Delhi and other cities, Chhillar has argued that private certification could compromise independent verification and deprive firefighters of crucial information about building layouts during emergencies. The petition has been filed through Advocates B Shravanth Shanker and Shivam Kunal. Advocate Avishkar Singhvi argued the case. The Delhi government was represented through its Standing Counsel Sameer Vashisht.

A Bench of Justices MM Sundresh and PB Varale made the remark while hearing an anticipatory bail plea by a man accused in a case involving the alleged recovery of a "huge quantity" of Ganja. items.title: DUSU election candidate can't be disqualified for membership in political party's student wing: Delhi HC
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Wednesday disposed of a public interest litigation (PIL) alleging that the ongoing Delhi University Students’ Union (DUSU) elections were being interfered with by political parties [Ms Vijeta v. Union of India & Ors] . A Bench of Chief Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya and Justice Tejas Karia noted that the primary contention of the petitioner was that some candidates were associated with student wings of political parties and that they would, therefore, be disqualified by contesting in the polls. The petitioner claimed that this is a clear violation of the Lyngdoh Committee’s rules governing student elections, particularly the rule mandating non-involvement of political parties. However, the Bench opined that the membership of a student candidate in a student wing of a political party is not an automatic ground for disqualification. What is barred by the Lyndgoh Committee rules is the involvement of members of political parties in student body elections and representation. " In our opinion, unless and until any one, maybe a student, who is a member of a political party as defined under the Representation of People Act participates in the election process, merely the fact of membership in the student wing of the political party, would not amount to association of such a student with the political party and, therefore, it will not in itself a violation of clause 6.3 or 6.3.1 of the Lyngdoh Committee recommendations ", the Court said. However, the Court cautioned University authorities and the Chief Election Officer that it is their responsibility to ensure that the elections remain free from interference by members of political parties. Chief Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya and Justice Tejas Karia The plea, filed by DU student Vijeta, alleged that the University failed to implement the Supreme Court's directions on keeping student elections free from political party influence. The plea alleged that student wings of political parties, including the National Students' Union of India (NSUI), the Akhil Bharatiya Vidyarthi Parishad (ABVP), the Aam Aadmi Party's (AAP's) student wing Association of Students for Alternative Politics (ASAP) and an alliance between Students' Federation of India (SFI) and the All India Students' Association (AISA), issued panels or declared candidates for the DUSU elections. items.title: Satya Niketan building collapse is a result of callous and criminal conduct: Delhi High Court
items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Wednesday remarked that the Satya Niketan paying guest (PG) building collapse, which led to the death of seven people, was a result of callous and criminal conduct. A Division Bench of Chief Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya and Justice Tejas Karia pointed to an article in The Indian Express about four students who lost their lives in the collapse. “It’s not an ordinary incident of any mishap. These four students had come to the capital city with lots of hopes and dreams. They came from small towns. All of that has been shattered by such a callous and criminal conduct on the part of...Who doesn’t know the problem of hostel in the city? Students are flocking to Delhi for higher education and this is not a new phenomenon. It has been happening for 20-25 years in the hope that they will build their career. See what has happened,” the Court remarked. Chief Justice Devendra Kumar Upadhyaya and Justice Tejas Karia The High Court made the remark while hearing a public interest litigation (PIL) filed by one Aakarshak Danveer Rathi regarding the incident. The Court said that it will hear the matter on September 25, when other matters related to the case are listed for consideration. The Satya Niketan building near Delhi University‘s South Campus collapsed on September 6. It was being used as a PG accommodation for boys before it caved in during repair work. Students and workers are among those dead. The Court is already considering a public interest litigation (PIL) seeking ₹1 crore compensation for the kin of the victims of the collapse besides a structural audit of all PG accommodations/hostels. It is also seized of another PIL seeking directions to ensure that each and every college affiliated to DU has hostel facilities for students.

items.title: Supreme Court criticises States for poor implementation of directions on menstrual hygiene at schools
items.summary: The Supreme Court recently expressed discontent with the inadequate implementation of its earlier directives to ensure the introduction of menstrual hygiene facilities in schools across the country [ Dr Jaya Thakur v. Government of India and Others ]. The Bench of Justices JB Pardiwala and R Mahadevan found that several States and Union Territories (UTs) had treated the matter as an mere formality and submitted compliance reports without any application of mind. “ Having carefully gone through the reports by the States/UTs, we are constrained to say that we are discontent with the manner in which compliance is reported. The response by some States exhibit non-application of mind or rather mere formality. For instance, where the response shall be subjective, some States have indicated compliance through mere statistics or objective yes/no responses, ” the Court said in an order passed on September 1. Justice JB Pardiwala and Justice R Mahadevan Notably, in a judgment pronounced on January 30 this year , the Court had ruled that the right to life under Article 21 of the Constitution includes the right to menstrual health. The Court further directed the nationwide implementation of the Union government’s Menstrual Hygiene Policy for school-going girls and prescribed mandatory standards for government and private schools. It had directed States and Union Territories to ensure that schools have functional gender-segregated toilets with running water, toilets accessible to children with disabilities, free sanitary napkins, menstrual hygiene management (MHM) corners, covered bins and safe waste-disposal systems. The Court has, since then, been monitoring compliance with these directions. On May 25, the Court sought fresh reports on the progress made in implementing its directions. In response, the Union government filed a consolidated affidavit on August 31. After examining the affidavit, the Court acknowledged that some progress had been made but found that several claims of complete compliance were contradicted by the States’ own data. Some States claimed complete compliance even though not all schools had accessible or gender-segregated toilets, handwashing facilities, sanitary-napkin vending machines or waste-disposal systems. The Court also noted that Punjab’s data was illegible. items.title: CIC orders DU Faculty of Law to justify withholding of exam evaluation records
items.summary: The Central Information Commission (CIC) has directed the Delhi University (DU) Central Public Information Officer (CPIO) to justify why records on how the Faculty of Law evaluates semester exam answer scripts were withheld. [Rishabh Mishra v, The CPIO, University of Delhi] Responding to the CPIO's argument that many of the appellant's queries were really seeking clarifications or opinions rather than facts, Information Commissioner Sudha Rani Relangi held that a CPIO cannot be compelled to answer for reasoning that isn't on record. "The CPIO is not required to create information, give an opinion, interpret records, or furnish explanations which are not available on the record," the Commission said. However, it clarified that existing records such as marking schemes, written instructions to examiners, notices, circulars and guidelines do constitute information under Section 2(f) of the Right to Information (RTI) Act, subject to exemptions under Section 8 or Section 9. Sudha Rani Relangi The CPIO had submitted that the evaluation process was confidential and held in a fiduciary capacity. The Commission held that the mere description of information as 'confidential' does not, by itself, constitute a valid ground for denial under the RTI Act. It added that any denial must be traceable to a specific exemption under Section 8 or Section 9, and that the fiduciary exemption under Section 8(1)(e) cannot be invoked mechanically without the university establishing that relationship for the particular information sought. The order came on a second appeal under the RTI Act filed by one Rishabh Mishra. His application sought the marking scheme, examiner training records, safeguards to keep evaluators from knowing students' identities, quality checks on the evaluation process and details of any digital evaluation used for the Faculty of Law's three-year LLB semester exams. The CPIO forwarded the query to the Joint Registrar (Examinations) and told Mishra that a response from that office was still awaited. Dissatisfied, Mishra filed a first appeal. items.title: Stray dogs: Kerala HC to monitor implementation of Supreme Court directions every month
items.summary: The Kerala High Court on Wednesday said that it would monitor on a monthly basis whether local authorities are implementing the Supreme Court's directions on stray dogs across the State. [In Re: Compliance with the directions issued by the Supreme Court in Suo Motu Writ Petition (Civil) No(s) 5 of 2025 v The State of Kerala & ors] A Division Bench of Justice AK Jayasankaran Nambiar and Justice Preeta AK said that the suo motu case would be taken up on the third Thursday of every month at 1:45 PM. Justice jayashankar nambiar and Justice Preeta AK The present suo motu case was initiated by the High Court pursuant to the May 19 judgment of the Supreme Court on stray dogs. The Supreme Court had directed all High Courts in the country to register suo motu proceedings to continuously monitor the implementation of its directions. The directions dealt with, among other things, sterilisation and vaccination of stray dogs, implementation of Animal Birth Control (ABC) programmes, creation of shelters and measures for dealing with rabid and aggressive dogs. Pursuant to the directions, the Kerala government constituted a high-level monitoring committee to oversee compliance. While hearing the matter, the Court said that the committee should examine the extent of compliance by each local authority and place a report before the Court by the 10th of every month. The Court also said that the committee must submit compliance reports separately classifying local authorities based on whether there was full compliance, part compliance or no compliance of the Supreme Court directions. It added that in cases of part compliance, the report should specify what remains to be done and the reasons for the same, while in cases where their is no compliance, the committee should mention the action being taken against such local authority for non-compliance. The Court also sought information on whether stray dog management committees (SDMCs) have been constituted in each local authority. " The other one is with regard to the Standard Operating Procedure with regard to dogs, euthanasia of dogs, rabid animals, the ones which are ferocious, etc. Details with regard to how many have been euthanised in each of these panchayats. So there is some accountability, " Justice Nambiar said. The Court stressed that if the committee identifies specific instance of non-compliance without justifiable reasons, the concerned local authorities would be called before the Court and action would be initiated

items.title: Supreme Court dismisses Central government's appeals against disability pension to ex-Army officers
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Tuesday dismissed a batch of around 271 appeals and special leave petitions filed by the Union government in cases concerning the grant of the disability element of service pension to several retired army officers [ Union of India v. Col NC Isaac ]. A Bench of Justices PS Narasimha and Alok Aradhe passed the ruling on challenges by the Union government to orders of the Armed Forces Tribunal (AFT) and High Courts granting relief to several retired army personnel who sought disability pension. Justice PS Narasimha and Justice Alok Aradhe The retired officers had approached the AFT/ High Courts after Release Medical Boards (RMBs) of the army classified their disabilities as neither attributable to nor aggravated by military service (NANA). This classification meant that the army was held not liable to pay the retired personnel disability pension, since the disability was neither caused nor worsened by their military service. After the AFT and High Courts overturned such classifications and granted the retired officers relief, the Central government challenged such rulings before the Supreme Court. By its September 15 ruling, the Court acknowledged that the Entitlement Rules of 2008 removed an earlier presumption that a person is physically fit when he joins military service. However, the Court ruled that this presumption would automatically mean that a disability detected when such an officer leaves the army is unconnected to military service. The Court rejected the Union's argument that the 2008 rules had fundamentally changed the earlier beneficial framework laid down in the Entitlement Rules of 1982. Ordinarily, the burden to prove that such an officer's disability is not attributable to or aggravated by military service would continue to lie on the employer (army), the Court ruled. " The mere addition of a causal requirement and a removal of the presumption that when a member joins service healthy, and, if, he leaves with a disability, it ought to be attributable to the military service, does not, by itself, change the core scheme of the Entitlement Rules 1982 because the other beneficial provisions broadly remain untouched ," it said. However, where a claimant approaches the relevant forum 15 or more years after discharge, retirement, invalidment or release, this burden shifts to the claimant, the Court added. items.title: Pre-ride tipping for cabs, autos under CCPA scanner: Why Rapido was fined but Namma Yatri wasn't
items.summary: The Central Consumer Protection Authority (CCPA) has come down on pre-ride tipping mechanisms used by cab and auto ride aggregators, holding that a tip sought before a journey begins can effectively become a payment for preferential or faster service rather than a voluntary gratuity. In two separate orders concerning Rapido and Namma Yatri, the consumer regulator examined features that encouraged passengers to pay above the quoted fare in the hope of getting a ride faster. While the CCPA imposed a ₹10 lakh penalty on Rapido for misleading advertisements, unfair trade practices and dark patterns, it closed proceedings against Namma Yatri after noting that the latter had removed the offending prompt before the show cause notice and subsequently disabled its “extra fare” feature altogether. The two cases arose from the same complaint received by the CCPA on May 16, 2025 regarding manipulative pre-ride tipping and pricing practices across ride-hailing platforms. In Rapido’s case, the Authority took exception to prompts such as: “ Captains aren’t accepting at ₹60. Try adding +10, +20, +30 .” The platform also displayed the message: “Higher the price, higher the chance of getting a ride.” The CCPA said the very premise of an “advance tip” was legally untenable since a tip is ordinarily paid after a service is rendered and assessed by the consumer. “ The very premise of ‘an amount over and above quoted fair’/‘advance tip’ is legally untenable, ” the order stated. It added that asking for such an amount before the service had even begun could make access to the service dependent on a consumer’s willingness and ability to pay more. The Authority also warned that such a mechanism could institutionalise price discrimination by giving lower priority to consumers unwilling or unable to pay over the quoted fare. It further found Rapido’s interface to amount to “confirm shaming” and “interface interference” under the Guidelines for Prevention and Regulation of Dark Patterns, 2023. Rapido was directed to discontinue such prompts and pay a ₹10 lakh penalty. A similar issue arose in the Namma Yatri case, where the app displayed: “ High Demand, adding a tip helps you find a ride faster .” The investigation found that the prompt nudged consumers to pay extra and could disadvantage those who did not tip. items.title: Delhi HC says words used by Ajeet Bharti were offensive, reserves order on anticipatory bail plea

The complaint was filed by Balakram Bauddh, Delhi State President of the Azad Samaj Party (Kanshi Ram), over a video titled SB79: Reservation Hatao Andolan Nautanki & More | Saptahik Bakaiti published on Bharti's social media handle. items.title: Karnataka HC notice to State in contempt plea for not paying illegally arrested homestay owner ₹5 lakh
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court on Wednesday sought the State government's response to a contempt of court plea alleging non-compliance with a direction to pay ₹5 lakhs as compensation to a Kodagu homestay owner for illegally arresting him in a criminal case [ Palecanda Ponnappa @ Vishal v. Shalini Rajnesh & others ]. The homestay owner was earlier arrested on April 19, on allegations that he failed to report the rape of a US tourist who stayed at his homestay. However, in July, the High Court found that the arrest was illegally carried out and ordered the State to pay him ₹5 lakh as compensation for violating the homestay owner's fundamental rights. The Court later also quashed the criminal case against him altogether. The homestay owner, Palecanda Ponnappa alias Vishal, has now approached the High Court with a contempt of court petition, accusing the State of failing to comply with the July order directing that he be compensated for his illegal arrest. A Division Bench of Justice Jayant Banerji and Justice K B Geetha today notice on the plea to the Chief Secretary and Additional Chief Secretary of the Home Department. The Court has listed the matter next after three weeks. Justice Jayant Banerji and Justice K B Geetha Ponnappa contends by the July 15 order, a single judge Bench of the Court ordered the State to pay him compensation for the illegal arrest within four weeks from the date of receipt of the order. A certified copy of the judgment and order was received by the State through the office of the Additional Special Public Prosecutor on July 15 itself, Ponnappa submitted. The four-week period stipulated by the Court consequently expired on August 12, 2026, he added. He also says that he issued a notice to the State authorities on July 27, calling upon them to comply with the compensation direction. However, the amount has not been paid, and no explanation has been provided either, says Ponnappa's plea. Advocate Angad Kamat appeared for Ponnappa.

items.title: Delhi HC seeks Centre’s stand on PIL for checks on addictive features of social media platforms

Union of India & Ors ]. A Bench of Justice Nitin Wasudeo Sambre and Justice Amit Sharma asked the Centre's counsel to take instructions on whether it was considering the framing of a policy to address the issue. This was after Additional Solicitor General (ASG) Chetan Sharma told the Court urged the Court not to delve into the matter since it fell within the domain of government policy. " The petition can be treated as a representation. There can be a time bound schedule for the government (to examine such a representation)," he suggested. " How can we say, 'you frame policies in a time-bound manner'? If you are saying, then it is fine. Are you contemplating framing of a policy?" the Court asked in turn. ASG Sharma said he would have to get instructions on whether such a policy is being actively considered by the Central government. Justice Nitin Wasudeo Sambre and Justice Amit Sharma The PIL was filed by one Vikas Kathuria, a law professor at BML Munjal University. It raises concerns over features such as infinite scrolling, autoplay, algorithmically curated personalised feeds, notifications and engagement indicators such as “likes." According to the plea, these features are designed to capture and retain users' attention and encourage repeated engagement with platforms. It argues that this model can be particularly harmful to children and young persons because prolonged and excessive social media use can affect their mental health and well-being. The PIL sought the constitution of an expert committee to examine such design features and recommend measures to address their impact. The plea also sought directions to the Centre and other authorities to restrict, prohibit or regulate such features, besides the creation of a mental health redressal fund for users affected by them. items.title: Gurugram hit and run: Court remands accused Kalyan Bainsla to police custody for two days
items.summary: A Gurugram court on Wednesday remanded Kalyan Bainsla, the driver accused of hitting a woman biker, to the custody of Gurugram police for two days. The Court also remanded Bainsla's cousin, Lavneesh, to police custody. The accused were produced before Judicial Magistrate Ist Class (JMIC) Nidhi Beniwal . While allowing the prosecution's application for remand of two days, the Court said, "Since in the present case, the accused persons are alleged to be involved in commission of offences punishable under Sections 281, 125, 78, 79, 109(1) and 3(5) BNS and arrest of co-accused has to be got effected on their identification and they are required to be interrogated in depth in the present case." Gurugram Court The Court directed the police to get the accused medically examined before and after the remand. They will be produced before the Court again on September 18. Both the accused had been arrested from Rajasthan and brought to Gurugram on Tuesday. The accused have been arrested in a case registered by the Sector 55/56 Police Station under Sections 109 (attempt to murder), 281 (rash driving) and 125 (act endangering life or personal safety of others) of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS). In the application moved before the magistrate today, the police also mentioned Section 78 (stalking) and 79 (word, gesture or act intended to insult the modesty of a woman) of the BNS. The case was registered after the victim, Shivani Chauhan, posted a video on social media on Sunday showing a vehicle allegedly driven by Bainsla, a gym owner, speeding towards her and hitting her bike on the Golf Course Road. The video was captured by a camera mounted on the bike. Chauhan, who goes by the name Sia on social media, is seen falling from her bike after the collision. She has accused Bainsla, referred to as Kalyan Singh in the court records, of harassing her before hitting her bike and of fleeing the spot after causing the accident. After the video went viral on social media, the police registered a suo motu case in the matter. However, the police initially did not invoke the offence of attempt to murder. It was later that Section 109 of the BNS was added to the case. The incident sparked national outrage with people demanding strict action against the car driver. Additional Public Prosecutor Dr Sumitra represented the police. Advocates Bhadresh Harikant, Payal Khatana and Harish Khatana represented accused Kalyan Singh. Advocate Bharat Singh Khatana represented accused Lavneesh.

items.title: Courts must take progressive approach in John Doe suits, can't insist on identifying unknown parties: Kerala HC
items.summary: The Kerala High Court recently calls on trial courts to take a progressive approach while dealing with John Doe suits, and not insist on the identification of unknown parties before such civil suits are entertained. [ Cubes Entertainments v Big Tree Entertainment Pvt Ltd & ors ] 'John Doe' suits (often referred to as 'Ashok Kumar’ suits in India) are civil proceedings filed against unidentified or anonymous legal opponents (defendants). Through such proceedings, a person filing the civil case (plaintiff) can sue unknown wrongdoers who can be identified and impleaded to the suit later. In a ruling passed on September 14, the High Court acknowledged that Order VI Rule 14A of the Code of Civil Procedure(CPC), 1908, usually requires plaintiffs to disclose the details and the address of defendants against whom a civil suit is filed. However, it pointed out that such identification of defendants becomes impossible when they are unknown, as is the case in John Doe suits. Justice Easwaran S emphasised that courts must keep up with the growing use of such 'John Doe' proceedings and not allow the CPC’s procedural requirements to defeat such legal action.. Since the film’s producer, Cubes Entertainment (plaintiff) did not know the exact identities of those who had posted the reviews, they were arrayed as 'John Doe/Ashok Kumars' in the suit. items.title: Karnataka HC upholds eviction of doctor from home over harassment of his 82-year-old mother
items.summary: The Karnataka High Court has upheld the eviction of a government doctor from his residence after his 82-year-old mother alleged that he and his wife were harassing her and interfering with her peaceful life [ Dr. M S Mahesh v. Deputy Commissioner ]. Justice Suraj Govindaraj took note of Section 22 of the Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act, 2007. Among other provisions, this Section calls on the State to to frame an action plan for the protection of life and property of senior citizens. The High Court held that the expression "protection of life and property of senior citizens” under Section 22 is wide enough to protect a senior citizen's enjoyment of her home. The Bench added that the statutory protection extends beyond the mere payment of maintenance and can include removing any source of harassment from a senior citizen's residence where the facts justify such action. “For a senior citizen, it carries with it the right to live with dignity, and that includes the right to reside peacefully in her own home without fear, harassment or humiliation,” the Court said in its August 6 order. Justice Suraj Govindraj The Court proceeded to dismiss a petition filed by a doctor challenging orders passed by the Assistant Commissioner and Mysuru Deputy Commissioner directing his eviction from the residential premises he shared with his aged mother. The said orders was passed on a plea by the mother seeking protection under the Maintenance and Welfare of Parents and Senior Citizens Act. The Court directed the Assistant Commissioner to implement the eviction orders within 60 days. The proceedings arose after one, Dr. MS Mahesh's mother, Subhadramma, approached the Assistant Commissioner in April 2023, alleging harassment at the Mysuru house. She alleged that her son had wrongfully confined her and her sister by locking them in a dark room and that Mahesh's wife was repeatedly picking quarrels with her, depriving her of a peaceful life. The Assistant Commissioner ordered Dr. Mahesh and his family to vacate the premises on August 12, 2024. The Deputy Commissioner subsequently dismissed Dr. Mahesh's appeal and affirmed the eviction order on February 4, 2025. Dr. Mahesh then approached the High Court, which rejected his plea and confirmed the eviction orders. items.title: CJP Protests: Supreme Court refuses to reconstitute panel probing violence

A Bench of Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana declined an application filed by certain parties to reconstitute the HPEC noting that their objections to the panel were premature. items.title: Plea in Karnataka High Court challenges State order on singing only 2 stanzas of Vande Mataram
items.summary: A Public Interest Litigation (PIL) petition has been filed before the Karnataka High Court against State government‘s recent order mandating that only first two stanzas of national song Vande Mataram be sung at State functions [Girish Bharadwaj v State of Karnataka] . The PIL has been filed by advocate Girish Bharadwaj who will be represented by advocate Angad Kamath. It is likely to be mentioned for an urgent hearing on Wednesday. On September 8, the State government mandated that only the first two stanzas of Vande Mataram be sung at State government functions. The order, however, provides an exception for programmes where the President, Vice-President, Prime Minister or Governor are in attendance and permits all 6 stanzas be sung in such programmes. Stating that the Parliament recently enacted the Prevention of Insults to National Honour (Amendment) Act, 2026 to include Vande Mataram as a national song and provide it with similar status as the national anthem, the PIL contends that the government order has undermined the parliament's intent to protect the full version of the song. The cabinet issued the order after an 'informal discussion' which was not supplemented by legal advice or by a cabinet Note of the administrative department, the PIL states. It further argues that government order is restrictive of the citizens' fundamental right of freedom of speech and expression under Article 19(1)(a) of the Constitution. It also contends that national symbols such as the national song can only be legislated on by the parliament with its residuary powers under Article 248 and Entry 97, List I of the Seventh Schedule, Indian Constitution which empowers the parliament to legislate on subjects not mentioned in the State (List II) or Concurrent List (List III). It further states that the State's order violates Article 256 which obliges States to comply with laws made by the parliament and Article 257(1) that mandates the State's executive powers to not obstruct or prejudice the Union's exercise of executive power. items.title: Shocking opaqueness: Delhi HC slams ITAT for passing order in Patanjali case without application of mind
items.summary: The Delhi High Court recently quashed 7 orders passed by the Income Tax Appellate Tribunal (ITAT) in a batch of cross-appeals involving Patanjali Ayurved Limited, stating that they portray a “shocking picture” of the procedural lapses and opaqueness in which the ITAT is functioning [Pr Commissioner of Income Tax, Central 1 Delhi v Patanjali Ayurved Limited] . A Division Bench of Justices Dinesh Mehta and Rajneesh Kumar Gupta was dealing with a batch of appeals filed by the Principal Commissioner of Income Tax, Central-1, Delhi, against Patanjali Ayurved. The case arose from 7 appeals before the ITAT relating to assessment years 2013-14 to 2015-16 and 2017-18. After examining the ITAT order, the High Court said that it reflected that the Tribunal had been passing orders in “over-anxiety” of disposing of the matters. “In the order under consideration, where the learned Members of the Tribunal have neither dealt with any contention of the assessee nor have, they discussed the issues involved in the appeals and disposed of seven appeals, vide an order which does not even contain seven paragraphs. We are not much concerned with the size of the order but what shocks us is, the non-application of mind and undue haste which learned Members of the Tribunal have exhibited,” the Court said. Justices Dinesh Mehta and Rajneesh Kumar Gupta The Court noted that the Tribunal orders recorded contradictory dates of hearing and pronouncement for different sets of appeals within the same batch. “On perusal of the impugned order, we are unable to comprehend anything out of it, as it is bereft of any logic, reasoning or rationale behind it. Apart from the procedural lacuna, we fail to understand that how a common order can be passed and released in relation to four appeals, which were heard and qua which the order was pronounced on 06.08.2025, whereas other three appeals were heard and order was pronounced on 13.08.2025,” the Court observed. Therefore, the High Court set aside all 7 orders and asked the President of the ITAT to ensure that cases are heard afresh by another bench. It also sent its order to the Secretary of the Ministry of Law and Justice for information. Senior Standing Counsel (SSC) Puneet Rai along with Advocates Ashvini Kr, Rishabh Nangia, Nikhil Jain and Nancy Jain represented the Income Tax Department. items.title: Second wife unaware of husband's existing marriage to first wife can't face bigamy charge: Madras HC
items.summary: The Madras High Court recently observed that a woman who marries a man without knowing that his earlier marriage is still subsisting cannot be prosecuted for bigamy under Section 82 of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS) [ Rajalakshmi v. State ]. Justice N Ramesh made the observation while granting anticipatory bail to a woman named Rajalakshmi, who was named as the second accused in a bigamy case. “ On the plain language of the (provision punishing bigamy), the offender is the person who already has a living spouse; a person who is herself unmarried and marries such a person, without knowledge of the subsisting marriage, does not thereby become an offender under Section 82," the Court observed. Therefore, the Court expressed reservations about whether the bigamy case could stand against Rajalakshmi at all. This was one of the factors that led the Court to grant her anticipatory bail. It, however, clarified that these are prima facie observations made to examine whether anticipatory bail should be given, and not comments on the merits of the allegations. She argued that she was herself a victim of his deception and had been unnecessarily implicated in a matrimonial dispute between him and the complainant. items.title: Delhi High Court asks RBI to mediate PayU's dispute with banks and Visa over merchant codes
items.summary: The Delhi High Court has asked the Reserve Bank of India (RBI) to mediate a dispute between PayU Payments, Yes Bank, ICICI Bank and Visa over the classification of merchants. In an order passed on September 14, Justice Subramonium Prasad directed the RBI to depute a senior officer familiar with the payments sector to try to resolve the dispute within 30 days. The Court also ordered the parties to maintain status quo on the disputed past transactions during the mediation. “In the opinion of this Court, adopting this process will ensure that the future transactions by the parties in the scheduled course are not hampered pending mediation and in the opinion of this Court, the senior officer of the RBI would be the most competent person to assist the parties to come to a solution pending the mediation process,” the Court said. The Bench reasoned that since the entire regime is being operated under the certificates granted by the RBI and under the supervision of the RBI, it would be more appropriate to request the RBI to act as a mediator instead of sending the parties to pre-litigation mediation. Justice Subramonium Prasad The dispute relates to Merchant Category Codes (MCCs), four-digit codes identifying a merchant’s principal business and used to determine the applicable interchange fee. ICICI Bank, which issues Visa cards, alleged that some merchants using PayU were assigned incorrect MCCs, resulting in lower interchange fees. It consequently raised claims against the acquiring banks through Visa’s Interchange Reimbursement Fee (IRF) process. PayU, however, said it does not assign MCCs. It collects and verifies merchants’ business information and forwards it to the acquiring bank, which independently assigns the appropriate code. Therefore, it disputed liability for any alleged misclassification. PayU approached the High Court after Yes Bank deducted amounts from its settlements towards the alleged IRF liability. items.title: Supreme Court agrees to hear plea by Wildlife CEO seeking protection in leopard poaching case
items.summary: The Supreme Court on Tuesday agreed to urgently hear a petition filed by Wildlife SOS co-founder and CEO Kartick Satyanarayan challenging a Madhya Pradesh High Court order that withdrew his interim protection from arrest in an alleged leopard poaching case. A Bench of Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana agreed to list the plea this week after Senior Advocate Siddhartha Dave mentioned the matter for urgent hearing. Chief Justice of India Surya Kant and Justices Joymalya Bagchi and V Mohana The case stems from a probe initiated by the Madhya Pradesh State Tiger Strike Force (STSF) concerning the alleged poaching of leopards, whose skins were recovered in Agra, Uttar Pradesh. The Madhya Pradesh High Court had recently dismissed two petitions filed under the Wildlife (Protection) Act, 1972. It revoked Satyanarayan's interim protection on alleged non-cooperation and directed him to appear before the STSF on September 21. According to a report , the High Court's Gwalior Bench recalled the relief after the Madhya Pradesh Forest Department alleged that Satyanarayan suppressed a third summons and an arrest warrant issued against him, while failing to join the probe into the poaching of 10 leopards across Sheopur and Morena districts. Rejecting the State's classification of Satyanarayan as "absconding," Wildlife SOS maintained that its anti-poaching unit had originally assisted in busting the racket, asserting that seeking legitimate legal protection does not amount to a refusal to cooperate. While mentioning the matter today, Dave submitted, "Two petitions have been dismissed by the High Court under the Wildlife Protection Act. We are from an NGO and we had led to the recovery of leopard skins. Now we ourselves have been implicated by the State." "You were keeping leopards at home?" CJI Kant asked. Dave clarified, "No. We led to the recovery of the skins in Agra. The recovery was in Uttar Pradesh, and the matter was thereafter taken up in Madhya Pradesh. We are willing to cooperate and appear before the authorities, but we need protection." Dave added that protection was necessary across related proceedings. "There is no point in appearing in one matter with protection if I can be arrested in the other." Acceding to the request, CJI Kant said, "It will be listed." items.summary: The Delhi High Court on Monday granted bail to a man accused of waging war against the government of India, observing that he has been in jail as an undertrial for almost eight years and the trial against him was far from over [ Mohammad Saqib@ Saqib Iftekar vs NIA ]. The Court observed that the trial in the case was unlikely to end soon and Saqib had already spent around eight years in jail. items.title: Contracts, institutions must ensure infrastructure disputes do not escalate and disrupt projects: CJI Surya Kant
items.summary: Chief Justice of India (CJI) Surya Kant on Monday said that disagreements arising from infrastructure projects should be addressed at an early stage, before they disrupt projects and develop into legal disputes. He called for India’s infrastructure ecosystem to shift from “retrospective justice”, which resolves disputes after the damage has occurred, to “preventive justice”, under which contracts and institutions are designed to prevent disagreements from escalating. " What our infrastructure ecosystem therefore needs is a shift from retrospective justice to preventive justice, " the CJI said. CJI Kant was delivering the keynote address at the International Federation of Consulting Engineers (FIDIC) Global Infrastructure Conference 2026 in New Delhi. “ The rule of law is not just about correcting the wrong but also about creating conditions where things go right, ” he said. The CJI explained that infrastructure contracts should clearly define the parties’ obligations and powers, distribute risks fairly and establish credible mechanisms for resolving disagreements promptly. “ A bridge cannot pause construction while an arbitration proceeds. A highway cannot wait for an appeal to run its course and a power project cannot suspend its economic purpose while the parties debate the meaning of a force majeure clause, ” he said. CJI Kant added that early intervention, open communication and swift decisions could prevent disagreements from turning into formal legal claims. “ The finest compliment to a dispute resolution mechanism is not that it has resolved many disputes, but that the project it served had so little need to use it, ” he said. items.title: Guntur police or the FBI? Andhra cops’ X takedown request sparks ridicule
items.summary: Follow TNM's WhatsApp channel for news updates and story links. A request sent by the Guntur Urban Police to social media platform X (formerly Twitter) seeking the removal of certain posts has drawn ridicule after the department identified itself as the ‘FBI’ in the submission. The matter surfaced after YSR Congress Party (YSRCP) member Nagarjuna Yadav, who uses the X handle @ImYanamala, received an email from X on July 28 informing him that law enforcement authorities had flagged three of his posts for allegedly violating Indian law. The email stated that X had received a request from the “FBI” concerning his account. The posts related to alleged irregularities in the District Selection Committee (DSC) recruitment process. The three posts criticised the handling of the recruitment process and alleged a lack of transparency. One called for a protest by unemployed youth, while another questioned why Nara Lokesh had not resigned over the alleged irregularities. A third urged Chief Minister N Chandrababu Naidu to dismiss his son from the Cabinet. ఏపీలో మరో "జెన్-జీ" (Gen-Z) ఉద్యమం మొదలవ్వబోతోంది! ఏళ్ల తరబడి కష్టపడి చదివిన నిరుద్యోగ యువత ఓపిక నశించింది. DSC అక్రమాలు, ప్రశ్నాపత్రాల లీకేజీ ఆరోపణలు, పారదర్శకత లేని విధానాలపై యువత రోడ్డుపైకి వచ్చే సమయం వచ్చింది! ఇప్పటికైనా చంద్రబాబు ప్రభుత్వం కళ్ళు తెరవాలి... విద్యాశాఖ… — Nagarjuna Yadav (@ImYanamala) July 26, 2026 Wondering why the American Federal Bureau of Investigation would object to his tweets, Yadav contacted X and asked for details of the agency that had submitted the request. In its response on September 13, X said the request had actually been submitted using the official government email address guntururbansp-ap@gov.in. The platform said the request was submitted by an individual identifying himself as Inspector AV Bramham but the organisation field reportedly carried the name “FBI”. X said its earlier reference to the FBI was an error caused by the information entered in the request. It specifically clarified that the communication had not originated from the United States’ Federal Bureau of Investigation. The Guntur SP did not answer our calls. items.title: AI is supercharging money scams – here’s what you can do to protect yourself
items.summary: For years, warnings about artificial intelligence and cybersecurity have focused on corporate networks and government systems. Those threats are real. But if you follow the money in the FBI’s fraud data, a different picture emerges: Staggering sums are flowing out of household accounts . In its 2025 annual report , the FBI’s Internet Crime Complaint Center began tracking complaints with an AI connection for the first time. Americans filed more than 22,000 such cases and reported roughly US$893 million in losses. Investment fraud accounted for $632 million of that, and people over 60 accounted for $352 million of the losses. Those figures include only victims who reported to the FBI, and only cases where AI’s role could be identified. The consulting firm Deloitte projects that the actual hit from AI will be much bigger and help push U.S. fraud losses overall to $40 billion by 2027, up from $12.3 billion in 2023. I’m a finance professor who studies household finance and how people use AI to make money decisions . And I believe the most consequential AI security story right now isn’t unfolding in server rooms, but at kitchen tables. Old cons, new machinery None of these scams are new. What AI changed is the cost and the quality of the cons. Cloning a voice now takes a few seconds of audio and cheap consumer tools. In one study , listeners were able to identify an AI-generated voice only about 60% of the time. Video is heading the same way. In 2024, a finance employee at the architecture and design firm Arup was tricked into wiring about $25 million to fraudsters after they set up a video meeting “staffed” by deepfakes of the chief financial officer and several colleagues. Phishing has improved, too. Clumsy wording and odd formatting used to give fraudulent emails away. Language models now write clean, fluent messages and can personalize them at scale using details scraped from social media. Deepfake videos of well-known business figures pitch bogus trading platforms. The same pressure is visible in business losses. items.title: How South Korea is tackling its super‑aging problem – and what other aging nations can learn from its experience
items.summary: In December 2024, the share of South Koreans ages 65 and older surpassed 20% for the first time, making it what demographers like us call a “ super-aged society .” By August 2026 that share had risen further , to 22.1%. That label can sound like a diagnosis, but population aging is not inherently a problem . In part, it reflects demographic progress: Fewer people are dying prematurely, and people are living longer due to improved living conditions. Thus, an older population can simply be a sign of society having grown safer, healthier and demographically more mature. The central concern, then, is not simply that a population is aging, but how quickly it is aging and whether society is prepared for it. South Korea moved from an aging society , meaning 7%-13% of a population is over 64, to a super-aged society in about 24 years. This transition was considerably faster than Japan, where it took 35 years. In the United States, older adults are projected to make up 23.4% of the population by 2060 . By 2060, about 41% of South Koreans are projected to be 65 or older, which would place the country to become the oldest . The country will face growing pressure on pensions, healthcare, workplaces and caregiving systems, but will have relatively little time to adapt. We research population health and aging . In our most recent study, published in July 2026, we examined how South Korea is dealing with its aging population . South Korea is not the first country to become a super-aged society, but the pace of its demographic transition has been exceptionally rapid. We believe its experience offers an early view of the choices many societies will soon face. Changing family life In the 1990s, the largest age groups were those between 15 and 34. Now, more than 30 years later, the youngest of these are more than 45 years old, and the oldest have already reached retirement age, which in South Korea is 60. Notably, the share of people ages 30 and younger is shrinking. South Korea’s aging is also connected to a broader shift in fertility, family formation and family life. As people gain greater individual autonomy in deciding how to organize their lives, there is a demographic transition toward sustained low fertility , later marriage and parenthood, and more diverse family arrangements. items.title: Private players should not replicate ISRO’s efforts: G Madhavan Nair writes
items.summary: India is at an important transition point in its space programme. The country is moving from a predominantly government-led space programme to an ecosystem in which private companies and startups can participate across the entire value chain. Indian Space Policy 2023 explicitly enables private entities to undertake activities including satellite realisation and operations, launch services, data acquisition and dissemination and ground infrastructure. ​The number of registered space startups has risen from one in 2014 to approximately 440 in 2026​, the government told the Rajya Sabha in August. The government also estimates India’s space economy at approximately US$9 billion in 2026, and predicts this will multiply to US$40–45 billion over the next decade. The question therefore is not whether India should encourage private participation in the space sector – the answer is obvious. But it is important to decide where Indian startups should concentrate their resources, so that they create sustainable businesses, and not mere technological demonstrations or duplication of what Indian Space Research Organisation (ISRO) has already done. India’s space programme has accumulated enormous technological knowledge, infrastructure and human expertise over several decades. The objective of the private sector should not be to recreate this capability independently. Instead, startups should concentrate their energies on innovation, specialised technologies and new business models; downstream applications and commercialisation and customer-facing services. This would leave ISRO to focus on technology leadership and advanced R&D; manufacturing scale, quality systems and capital. Understandably, space hardware attracts the most attention because rockets and satellites are visible and technologically impressive. But the bigger economic value often lies downstream, when the data collected by the satellite is able to answer a customer’s question. The potential of satellite data is enormous, from estimating crop yield or drought monitoring to flood prediction, transmission line monitoring, forest fire monitoring and climate risk analysis. items.title: Nakkheeran journalist Prakash arrested for derogatory allegations against woman anchor
items.summary: The Chennai police on Wednesday, September 16, arrested journalist Damodaran Prakash, who works for Tamil investigative magazine Nakkheeran , for making derogatory remarks about a woman anchor who works with YouTuber Savukku Shankar. Prakash was arrested from his residence in Chintadripet, Chennai. According to the police, Prakash appeared in a video titled ‘HIV Savukku — Kalyanam’ which was published on YouTube in January this year, and made malicious rumours against the woman anchor saying that she had contracted HIV. The video, published on the YouTube channel King 24 X 7, featured the woman’s photograph and contained “false, disgusting statements regarding her personal life, thereby defaming womanhood,” police said. The case was registered at the S-8 Adambakkam Police Station based on a complaint filed by the woman. Police said Prakash was arrested under various sections of the Bharatiya Nyaya Sanhita (BNS), the Information Technology Act (IT Act) and the Tamil Nadu Prohibition of Harassment of Women Act (TNPHW Act). Police said that the person involved in moderating the programme had not yet been identified and that further investigation was underway. The Chennai Press Club has issued a statement condemning Prakash’s arrest and questioned the eight-month gap between the complaint and the police action. The Press Club alleged that the arrest appeared to be retaliatory in the wake of his anti-government views. In its statement, the Press Club said Prakash had played a significant role in several investigative stories published by Nakkheeran . It cited his work on the Sankararaman murder case, the disproportionate assets case against former Chief Minister J Jayalalithaa, the Pollachi sexual assault case and the death of a schoolgirl in Kallakurichi, among others. “Prakash, who has fearlessly pointed out and criticised the mistakes of those in positions of power, was arrested now for something he said on YouTube nearly eight months ago, without any prior inquiry. This raises several questions,” the Press Club said. “It also raises concerns over whether such action was taken to intimidate journalists who point out and criticise wrongdoing,” it added. The Press Club said it had no objection to legal action being taken against Prakash if the allegations against him were established. However, it strongly condemned his arrest without first seeking an explanation from him or conducting an inquiry, and urged the Tamil Nadu government to immediately release him.
